subject: social_science

concepts.title: Population Density
concepts.definition: The average number of individuals residing per unit of geographical area, typically calculated per square kilometer.
concepts.key_idea: Measures how crowded a region is by dividing its total population by its land area.
question_patterns: calculate the population density of a region with a population of {population} and an area of {area}
what is the population density if {population} people live in {area} square kilometers
find the average number of persons per square kilometer when population is {population} and area is {area}
determine the density of population given {population} residents and {area} sq km of land
compute the population density for an area of {area} square km containing {population} inhabitants

solution_steps.explain: The population density is found by dividing the total population by the area.

concepts.title: Absolute Population Increase
concepts.definition: The actual number of people added to a population over a specific period, calculated by subtracting the population at the start of the period from the population at the end.
concepts.key_idea: The net numerical growth in population size over a given timeframe.
question_patterns: find the absolute increase in population from {earlier_population} to {later_population}
calculate the magnitude of population growth if the initial population was {earlier_population} and the final population is {later_population}
how many people were added to the population if it grew from {earlier_population} million to {later_population} million
determine the absolute population growth between two censuses with populations of {earlier_population} and {later_population}
compute the net addition to the population when it increases from {earlier_population} to {later_population}

solution_steps.action: subtract earlier population from later population
solution_steps.explain: The absolute increase is the difference between the final population and the initial population.

concepts.title: Sex Ratio
concepts.definition: The demographic metric representing the number of females per one thousand males in a given population.
concepts.key_idea: An essential social indicator showing the gender balance in a society.
question_patterns: calculate the sex ratio of a region with {females} females and {males} males
what is the sex ratio if there are {females} females and {males} males in a community
find the number of females per 1000 males when the female population is {females} and male population is {males}
determine the sex ratio given {females} females and {males} males
compute the sex ratio for a town having {males} males and {females} females

solution_steps.action: divide females by males and multiply by 1000
solution_steps.explain: The sex ratio is calculated as the number of females per 1000 males.

concepts.title: Natural Increase of Population
concepts.definition: The difference between the birth rate and the death rate in a population, representing growth excluding migration.
concepts.key_idea: The net change in population resulting solely from births and deaths.
question_patterns: calculate the natural increase rate if the birth rate is {birth_rate} and the death rate is {death_rate}
what is the natural growth rate of a population with a birth rate of {birth_rate} per thousand and a death rate of {death_rate} per thousand
find the difference between a birth rate of {birth_rate} and a death rate of {death_rate}
determine the rate of natural increase given birth rate {birth_rate} and death rate {death_rate}
compute the natural population increase rate when birth rate is {birth_rate} and death rate is {death_rate}

solution_steps.action: subtract death rate from birth rate
solution_steps.explain: The natural increase is the birth rate minus the death rate.

concepts.title: Dependency Ratio
concepts.definition: The ratio of the dependent population (children below 15 and elderly above 59 years) to the economically active working-age population (15 to 59 years).
concepts.key_idea: Measures the economic burden on the productive portion of the population.
question_patterns: calculate the dependency ratio if there are {dependents} percent dependents and {working_age} percent working-age people
find the dependency ratio given {dependents} dependents and {working_age} working adults
what is the dependency ratio of a population with {dependents} total dependents and {working_age} active workers
determine the dependency ratio when the dependent group is {dependents} and the productive group is {working_age}
compute the dependency ratio for a population structure of {dependents} percent dependents and {working_age} percent working age

solution_steps.action: divide dependents by working age and multiply by 100
solution_steps.explain: The dependency ratio is the percentage of dependents relative to the working-age population.

concepts.title: Age Composition
concepts.definition: The classification of a population into distinct age groups, typically categorized as children, working age, and the elderly, which determines its socio-economic structure.
concepts.key_idea: The distribution of people across different age categories affects economic dependency and resource needs.
question_patterns: explain the three broad categories of age composition
what are the main age groups in a population
how does age composition affect the dependency ratio
describe the characteristics of the working age group in population structure
why are children and the aged considered dependent groups

solution_steps.explain: The population is grouped into children (under 15), working age (15-59), and aged (above 59).
Children and aged are economically dependent, while working age is productive.

concepts.title: Literacy Rate Criteria
concepts.definition: The standard by which a person is considered literate, defined in India as an individual aged 7 years or older who can read and write with comprehension in any language.
concepts.key_idea: Literacy requires being at least 7 years old and having the ability to read and write with understanding.
question_patterns: who is considered a literate person according to the Indian Census
what are the criteria for literacy in India
define the literacy rate as per the Census of India
at what age is a person eligible to be counted as literate
explain the definition of literacy used in the 2011 census

solution_steps.explain: A person must be at least 7 years old to be considered for literacy.
The person must be able to read and write with understanding in any language.

concepts.title: Occupational Structure
concepts.definition: The distribution of the economically active population across primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors of the economy.
concepts.key_idea: The proportion of workforce in different sectors indicates the level of economic development.
question_patterns: what is occupational structure
distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary activities
how does occupational structure vary between developed and developing countries
what percentage of India's population is engaged in agriculture
explain the shift in occupational structure in India

solution_steps.explain: Occupations are split into primary (agriculture, mining), secondary (manufacturing, construction), and tertiary (services, transport).
Developed nations have more people in secondary and tertiary sectors, while developing nations have more in primary.

concepts.title: National Population Policy (NPP 2000)
concepts.definition: A comprehensive policy framework initiated by India to address health, education, and family welfare, with special emphasis on adolescents, immunization, and compulsory schooling.
concepts.key_idea: A policy aiming to improve quality of life by promoting planned parenthood, education, and health.
question_patterns: what are the major features of the National Population Policy 2000
how does NPP 2000 address the needs of adolescents
what are the objectives of the Family Welfare Programme in India
explain the policy framework of NPP 2000 regarding education and health
how does the government plan to reduce infant mortality under NPP 2000

solution_steps.explain: NPP 2000 aims for free education up to age 14, reducing infant mortality, and universal immunization.
The policy targets adolescent nutrition, delayed marriage, and reproductive health awareness.
